obligation_plain_words: Run a documented, continuous, lifecycle risk management system: identify foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights (intended use AND reasonably foreseeable misuse), use post-market data, adopt targeted measures, and judge residual risk acceptable per hazard and overall.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 6.1.2 AI risk assessment; cl. 6.1.3 AI risk treatment; cl. 8.2-8.3 operational assessment/treatment; A.6.1.2 objectives for responsible development; A.6.1.3 processes for responsible design and development. Intent: a repeatable AI-risk process with treatment and residual-risk acceptance.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: cl. 6.1.2-6.1.3 (information-security risk assessment/treatment) - covers the security slice only.
residual_gap: ISO risk = effect of uncertainty on the organisation's objectives; Art. 9 risk = harm to health, safety, fundamental rights. A certificate does not show the risk criteria are rights-anchored. Art. 9(3) scoping, per-hazard AND overall residual-risk acceptability (9(5)), and foreseeable-misuse analysis are not explicit in ISO. Certification auditors do not test against Art. 9.
implementation_note: Re-base AIMS risk criteria on Art. 9(2) harm categories; keep per-hazard residual-risk records; feed the /register/ layer. NIST MANAGE 1.4 (residual risk to end users) is the closest single outcome to Art. 9(5).
harmonised_standard_pipeline: prEN 18228 (AI risk management): public enquiry closed 30 Jul 2026, rejected by a majority of national standards bodies; comment resolution due Nov 2026. Not cited in the OJ.

obligation_plain_words: Test the system to find the most appropriate risk measures: consistent performance for intended purpose, against metrics and probabilistic thresholds defined in advance, at any point in development and in any event before placing on the market (real-world testing optional under Art. 60).
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.4 AI system verification and validation; A.6.2.2 requirements and specification; cl. 8.1 operational planning. Intent: define and run V&V against stated criteria.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.29 Security testing in development and acceptance; 8.31 Separation of development, test and production environments.
residual_gap: ISO asks you to define V&V criteria but does not require pre-defined probabilistic thresholds or a pre-market gate. Nothing in either framework ties test metrics to the intended purpose in Art. 9(8) terms.
implementation_note: Write acceptance thresholds into the requirements spec (A.6.2.2) BEFORE testing; record them as evidence for Annex IV 2(g).

obligation_plain_words: When applying the risk management system, consider whether the system is likely to adversely affect people under 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.5.4 Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups of individuals; A.5.2 impact assessment process. Intent: look at effects on specific groups.
residual_gap: Neither framework names minors or vulnerable groups as a mandatory consideration; ISO A.5.4 is the right place but is generic.
implementation_note: Add an explicit minors/vulnerable-group question to the A.5.2 impact-assessment template.

obligation_plain_words: Apply data governance and management practices to training, validation and testing data: design choices, collection and origin (incl. original purpose of personal data), preparation operations, assumptions, availability/suitability, and identification of data gaps that prevent compliance.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: Art. 10(1) now cross-refers to Art. 4a; Art. 10(5) deleted
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.7.2 Data for development and enhancement; A.7.3 Acquisition of data; A.7.4 Quality of data; A.7.5 Data provenance; A.7.6 Data preparation; A.4.3 Data resources. Intent: managed, traceable data lifecycle.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets; 5.12 Classification of information.
residual_gap: 'Substantially' applies to the PROCESS. ISO A.7 sets no quality thresholds and is not tied to one system's intended purpose; Art. 10(2)(h) 'data gaps that prevent compliance with this Regulation' is a legal test ISO does not frame.
implementation_note: Produce one data sheet per system (also feeds Annex IV 2(d)); record 10(2)(h) data-gap analysis explicitly.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: prEN 18284 (quality and governance of datasets): drafting; Commission comments under review Aug 2026.

obligation_plain_words: Examine data for biases likely to harm health/safety, affect fundamental rights or cause prohibited discrimination (including feedback-loop bias); detect, prevent and mitigate them; keep data relevant, sufficiently representative and as error-free/complete as possible for the persons and setting concerned.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.7.4 Quality of data; A.5.4 Assessing impact on individuals or groups; A.6.2.4 V&V. Intent: data fit for purpose and group-level impact looked at.
residual_gap: Neither names 'prohibited discrimination under Union law' as the test. NIST MEASURE 2.11 is the most direct outcome in any of the three corpora but is evaluative, not a conformity threshold. Note statutory shortcut: Art. 42(1) presumes compliance with 10(4) for systems trained and tested on data reflecting the intended setting.
implementation_note: Document the bias metrics chosen and WHY (NIST 1.2.1 warns metrics can be gamed); keep the Art. 42(1) setting-representativeness evidence.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: prEN 18283 (bias management): drafting; WD consultation closed 30 Apr 2026; targeted for enquiry before Oct 2026 plenary.

obligation_plain_words: Exceptionally process special-category personal data for bias detection and correction only if strictly necessary, with no feasible alternative data, re-use limits, state-of-the-art security, controlled access, no onward transfer, prompt deletion, and a record of why it was necessary.
application_date: Applies from 27 Jul 2026 (entry into force of Reg. 2026/1744) per secondary sources; verify against OJ text.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: NEW: Art. 10(5) deleted; Art. 4a inserted (secondary sources only - OJ text not directly retrieved)
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.7.3 Acquisition of data. Intent: data is obtained deliberately. Does not address lawful basis for special-category data.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.34 Privacy and protection of PII; 8.3 Information access restriction; 8.10 Information deletion; 8.11 Data masking.
residual_gap: Neither AI framework supplies the GDPR Art. 9 analysis. 'Strict necessity' and 'no alternative data' are legal judgements for DPO + counsel. 27001 controls evidence the SECURITY conditions only.
implementation_note: Treat as a DPIA-linked decision record, not a control. Do not claim coverage from ISO 42001.

obligation_plain_words: Draw up technical documentation BEFORE placing on the market and keep it current, containing at least the Annex IV elements: description, development process, data sheets, human-oversight assessment, signed test reports, cybersecurity measures, RMS description, change log, list of harmonised standards applied, EU declaration of conformity copy, post-market plan.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: simplified Annex IV form extended from SMEs to small mid-caps (SMCs)
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.7 AI system technical documentation; A.6.2.3 Documentation of design and development; cl. 7.5 Documented information. Intent: maintain system-level documentation.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.37 Documented operating procedures; 5.33 Protection of records.
residual_gap: ISO does not prescribe Annex IV content. Specific gaps: list of harmonised standards applied (Annex IV pt 7), copy of EU declaration of conformity (pt 8), post-market plan inclusion (pt 9), dated and signed test reports (2(g)). NIST outcomes are deliberately non-prescriptive on documentation content.
implementation_note: Use Annex IV as the template and treat A.6.2.7 as the process that keeps it current.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: None dedicated; EN 18286 touches documentation via QMS (Art. 17(1)(k)).

obligation_plain_words: Design the system so it can technically record events (logs) automatically over its lifetime, sufficient to spot risk situations or substantial modification, support post-market monitoring and enable deployer monitoring.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.8 AI system recording of event logs. Intent: decide what events are recorded and retain them.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.15 Logging; 8.16 Monitoring activities; 8.17 Clock synchronization.
residual_gap: ISO A.6.2.8 asks the organisation to define logging; Art. 12 is a PRODUCT-DESIGN requirement (the capability must exist in the system). 27001 logging is built for security events, not AI-functioning traceability. 12(3) adds minimum fields for remote biometric identification.
implementation_note: Specify log schema in the requirements spec; verify it supports Art. 72 analysis and Art. 26(5) deployer monitoring.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: prEN 18229-1 (logging): enquiry closed 20 Aug 2026, rejected on the weighted population threshold; 443 comments; reconsideration requests due 25 Sep 2026.

obligation_plain_words: Make the system transparent enough for deployers to interpret and use its output, and ship instructions for use covering at least: provider identity, intended purpose, tested accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity levels and what can affect them, foreseeable misuse risks, explainability features, group-level performance, input-data specs, pre-determined changes, oversight measures, resource/lifetime needs and log-collection mechanisms.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.2 System documentation and information for users; A.8.5 Information for interested parties; A.6.2.7 Technical documentation. Intent: users get the information needed to use the system properly.
residual_gap: A.8.2 does not mandate the Art. 13(3) content list: declared accuracy metrics and circumstances that affect them, group-level performance, pre-determined changes, and deployer log-collection mechanisms are the usual omissions.
implementation_note: Build the instructions for use from the Art. 13(3) list, not from the A.8.2 intent summary.

obligation_plain_words: Design the system (with suitable human-machine interface) so natural persons can oversee it: understand its capacities and limits, stay aware of automation bias, interpret output, decide not to use or to override/reverse output, and intervene or stop it in a safe state ('stop' button or equivalent).
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.1.3 Processes for responsible design and development; A.6.2.2 Requirements and specification; A.3.2 AI roles and responsibilities. Intent: responsible design and defined accountability - no control addresses oversight interface design.
residual_gap: Art. 14 is a DESIGN requirement (override, stop, automation-bias awareness). ISO 42001 has no control for it. NIST is stronger than ISO here (MAP 3.5, MANAGE 2.4 'supersede, disengage, or deactivate') but still organisational, not a product-design test.
implementation_note: Specify oversight measures as functional requirements and test them; record in Annex IV 2(e).

obligation_plain_words: Achieve and maintain appropriate accuracy and robustness over the lifecycle; declare accuracy metrics in the instructions for use; be resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies (redundancy / fail-safe); for systems that keep learning, remove or reduce feedback loops that feed biased output back into input.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.4 AI system verification and validation; A.6.2.6 AI system operation and monitoring. Intent: validate before release, monitor in operation.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.14 Redundancy of information processing facilities; 8.13 Information backup; 8.6 Capacity management.
residual_gap: Neither framework sets levels; both require you to define and monitor them. Feedback-loop mitigation in continual-learning systems (15(4)) is not explicit in either. NIST 'Valid and Reliable' and 'Safe' characteristics are the closest conceptual fit.
implementation_note: Declare metrics once, in the instructions for use, and trace them to Annex IV 2(g) test reports.

obligation_plain_words: Be resilient against unauthorised third parties altering use, outputs or performance, with measures against data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples/model evasion, confidentiality attacks and model flaws.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: new Art. 42(3) - systems complying with Reg. (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) deemed to comply with Art. 15 cybersecurity (secondary source; verify)
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.4.5 System and computing resources; cl. 6.1.2 AI risk assessment. Intent: resourcing and risk assessment - no AI-specific security control exists in Annex A.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.8 Management of technical vulnerabilities; 8.25 Secure development life cycle; 8.26 Application security requirements; 8.29 Security testing; 5.7 Threat intelligence; 8.20 Networks security.
residual_gap: A generic ISMS does not name the Art. 15(5) AI-specific attack classes (poisoning, evasion, confidentiality attacks, model flaws). NIST AI RMF text (s.3.3) names them but as characteristics, not as a required test. Art. 42(2) presumption needs a certificate under an EU cybersecurity scheme (Reg. 2019/881) whose reference is published in the OJ.
implementation_note: Extend the 27001 threat model to ML-specific attacks and test them under A.6.2.4. This is where a 27001 + 42001 organisation is strongest.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: prEN 18282 (AI cybersecurity): enquiry rejected by national bodies 30 Jul 2026; new scope at ballot to 16 Sep 2026.

obligation_plain_words: Operate a documented quality management system covering 13 aspects: compliance strategy incl. conformity assessment and modification management; design/development control; test and validation; technical specs and standards applied; data management; risk management; post-market monitoring; serious-incident procedures; authority communication; record-keeping; resource management; accountability framework.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: Art. 17(2) proportionality extended to small mid-caps (SMCs)
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 4-10 (whole AI management system); cl. 5.2 AI policy; cl. 7.5 documented information; A.2.2 AI policy; A.3.2 roles; A.6.2.2-A.6.2.8 AI system life-cycle controls; A.10.3 suppliers. Intent: a certified management system around AI development and use.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: cl. 4-10 as the parallel ISMS (shared Annex SL structure) - supports integrated management-system operation.
residual_gap: The closest thing to an equivalence in the whole crosswalk, and it is still NOT equivalence. Missing from a stock ISO 42001 AIMS: (a) conformity-assessment/modification strategy, (e) which technical specs and standards apply and what you do where harmonised standards are not used, (i) Art. 73 serious-incident procedure, (j) authority/notified-body communication procedure. A certificate attests to the management system, not to Art. 17 conformity.
implementation_note: Add an 'Art. 17 overlay' to the AIMS for items (a), (e), (i), (j). Watch EN 18286 - it is the standard built for Art. 17 and reportedly includes an Annex D mapping to ISO 42001 controls.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: EN 18286:2026 published by CEN-CENELEC in July 2026 (sources differ: 22 and 30 Jul). Not cited in the OJ as of 15 Sep 2026 (latest source), so NO presumption of conformity yet.

obligation_plain_words: Retain automatically generated logs under the provider's control for a period appropriate to intended purpose and at least six months, unless other Union or national law (notably data protection) says otherwise.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.8 AI system recording of event logs. Intent: decide log content and keep it.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.15 Logging; 5.33 Protection of records.
residual_gap: The six-month floor and the data-protection override are legal parameters; the GDPR storage-limitation tension is for the DPO to resolve, not for a control to evidence.
implementation_note: Record the retention basis per log type, including the GDPR justification.

obligation_plain_words: Before placing on the market, put the system through the required conformity assessment: internal control (Annex VI), or QMS + technical documentation assessed by a notified body (Annex VII), or the sectoral procedure for Annex I products; repeat on substantial modification.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: Art. 43(3) revised for sectoral notified bodies (to apply for designation under the Act by 28 Jan 2028 - secondary source; verify)
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 9.2 Internal audit; cl. 9.3 Management review. Intent: the organisation audits its own management system.
residual_gap: Different object, different issuer, different legal effect: an ISO 42001 certificate attests a management system; Art. 43 assesses THE SYSTEM against Section 2. For Annex III point 1 (biometrics) the Annex VII notified-body route is mandatory where harmonised standards are not applied (Art. 43(1)) - and none is cited in the OJ yet.
implementation_note: Decide Annex VI vs VII per system early; do not present an ISO certificate as a conformity assessment.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: prEN 18285 (conformity assessment framework): mature draft 4 Sep 2026, going to the Commission.

obligation_plain_words: Draw up a written EU declaration of conformity per system (Annex V content), keep it 10 years, give copies to authorities on request. By signing, the provider assumes responsibility for Section 2 compliance.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
residual_gap: A legal act with legal consequences (47(4)). No management-system standard or voluntary framework produces it.
implementation_note: Template it from Annex V; sign only after the conformity assessment completes.

obligation_plain_words: Affix the CE marking (digital CE marking for digitally provided systems), followed by the notified-body number where one was involved.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
residual_gap: Statutory marking; outside the scope of every voluntary framework.
implementation_note: Operational/legal step after Art. 47.

obligation_plain_words: Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing on the market (national-level registration for Annex III point 2 critical infrastructure).
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.4.2 Resource documentation. Intent: know what resources/systems you have - not a regulatory registration.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets.
residual_gap: An internal AI-system inventory is a prerequisite for registration but is not registration.
implementation_note: Keep the inventory fields aligned to Annex VIII so registration is an export, not a project.

obligation_plain_words: If you conclude an Annex III system is NOT high-risk (e.g. narrow procedural task), document that assessment BEFORE placing on the market, register the system under Art. 49(2), and produce the assessment on request. Profiling of natural persons is always high-risk.
application_date: Art. 6(3)-(4): applies with the high-risk regime (2 Dec 2027); registration obligation retained
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Registration obligation retained despite earlier proposal to remove it (Cooley, secondary source); Commission Art. 6 guidelines draft published 19 May 2026 (Mayer Brown, secondary)
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.5.2 AI system impact assessment process. Intent: assess an AI system's impacts - no classification step exists in ISO 42001.
residual_gap: Classification is a legal determination. Neither framework has an Act-aligned classification step; a wrong 'not high-risk' conclusion is itself the exposure.
implementation_note: Keep a dated classification memo per system; revisit on any intended-purpose change (Art. 25(1)(c)).

obligation_plain_words: If you have reason to think a placed system is non-conforming, immediately take corrective action (bring into conformity, withdraw, disable or recall) and inform distributors, deployers, authorised representative and importers; if it presents a risk (Art. 79(1)), investigate with the deployer and inform market surveillance authorities and any notified body.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 10.2 Nonconformity and corrective action; A.8.4 Communication of incidents; A.6.2.6 Operation and monitoring. Intent: fix and learn from nonconformities and incidents.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.26 Response to information security incidents; 5.27 Learning from information security incidents.
residual_gap: ISO corrective action is raised against the management system; Art. 20 is triggered by non-conformity with the REGULATION and requires a real withdraw/disable/recall capability plus notification of authorities. 'Immediately' has no ISO equivalent.
implementation_note: Pre-build the withdraw/disable runbook and the authority-notification template (ties to PRV-HR-A73-SI).

obligation_plain_words: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system, proportionate to the technology and risk, based on a plan that forms part of the technical documentation; actively collect, document and analyse performance data over the system's lifetime to evaluate CONTINUOUS COMPLIANCE with Section 2, including interaction with other AI systems.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Date moved only. Commission template implementing act was due 2 Feb 2026 - verify whether adopted.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.6 AI system operation and monitoring; cl. 9.1 Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation; cl. 10.1 Continual improvement. Intent: monitor operation and improve.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.16 Monitoring activities.
residual_gap: NIST MANAGE 4.1 is the closest single outcome in any corpus, but neither framework frames monitoring as evaluating continuous compliance with the Section 2 requirements, and neither requires the plan to sit inside the technical documentation or to follow the Commission template.
implementation_note: Define monitoring KPIs as Section 2 compliance indicators (accuracy drift, log completeness, oversight overrides), not just performance.

obligation_plain_words: Report any serious incident to the market surveillance authority of the Member State where it occurred: immediately once a causal link (or reasonable likelihood) is established and in any event within 15 days of awareness; 2 days for widespread infringement or critical-infrastructure disruption; 10 days for a death; an incomplete initial report is allowed. Investigate, assess risk and do not alter the system before informing authorities.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Date moved only. Commission guidance was due 2 Aug 2025 (Art. 73(7)) - verify it was issued.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.4 Communication of incidents; A.8.3 External reporting; cl. 10.2. Intent: communicate incidents to the right parties.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.24 Incident management planning and preparation; 5.25 Assessment and decision on events; 5.26 Response; 5.27 Learning; 5.5 Contact with authorities.
residual_gap: An ISO 'incident' is not an Act 'serious incident' (death/serious health harm; critical-infrastructure disruption; infringement of fundamental-rights obligations under Union law; serious property/environment harm). The 15/10/2 day clocks and the no-alteration rule are not in any framework. Expect overlap with GDPR 72h and NIS2 clocks.
implementation_note: Add an 'Art. 3(49) classification' triage step and the three clocks to the incident procedure.

obligation_plain_words: Any distributor, importer, deployer or third party becomes the PROVIDER (with all Art. 16 duties) if it puts its name/trademark on a high-risk system, makes a substantial modification, or changes the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system (incl. a general-purpose AI system) so that it becomes high-risk. Suppliers of components/tools must agree in writing what information and technical access the provider needs.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: Art. 25(2) initial-provider cooperation duty restated (secondary source; verify)
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.10.2 Allocating responsibilities; A.10.3 Suppliers; A.10.4 Customers. Intent: responsibilities across the supply chain are defined and supplier requirements are managed.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.19 Information security in supplier relationships; 5.20 Addressing information security within supplier agreements; 5.21 Managing information security in the ICT supply chain; 5.22 Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services.
residual_gap: ISO A.10 evidences allocation and supplier management, but does not test the Art. 25(1) trigger: a deployer that rebrands or re-purposes a GPAI system for an Annex III use inherits full provider duties. That is the commonly missed exposure.
implementation_note: Add a 'would this change make us the provider?' gate to change management and to every procurement of a GPAI-based system.

obligation_plain_words: A provider established outside the EU must, before making a high-risk system available in the Union, appoint by written mandate an EU-established authorised representative with the Art. 22(3) tasks.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
residual_gap: A statutory appointment; no framework contains an equivalent.
implementation_note: Contract and mandate wording to follow Art. 22(3)(a)-(e).

obligation_plain_words: Providers take measures to support the AI literacy of staff and others operating or using AI systems on their behalf, in light of their knowledge, context of use and the people the systems are used on.
risk_tier: All AI systems (horizontal, Chapter I; outside the HR/GPAI scope boundary but included because it binds every provider)
application_date: Applied from 2 Feb 2025
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: duty changed from 'ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level' to 'take measures to support the development of' AI literacy; Commission/Member States to support (Reg. 2026/1744; verify OJ text and application date)
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 7.2 Competence; cl. 7.3 Awareness; A.4.6 Human resources; A.3.2 AI roles and responsibilities. Intent: people doing AI work are competent and aware.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 6.3 Information security awareness, education and training.
residual_gap: The softened wording makes the ISO competence/awareness clauses a good fit. Residual: Art. 4 also reaches 'other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf' (contractors), and ISO competence is scoped to persons affecting AIMS performance.
implementation_note: Extend the training record to contractors and to affected-persons context.

obligation_plain_words: Deployers take measures to support the AI literacy of staff and others operating or using AI systems on their behalf.
application_date: Applied from 2 Feb 2025
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 7.2 Competence; cl. 7.3 Awareness; A.9.2 Processes for responsible use of AI systems; A.4.6 Human resources.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 6.3 Information security awareness, education and training.
residual_gap: As provider row. Deployer-specific: literacy must cover how to interpret THIS system's output (ties to Art. 14(4) and Art. 26(2)).
implementation_note: Tie training content to the provider's instructions for use.

obligation_plain_words: Take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use the high-risk system in accordance with the provider's instructions for use.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.9.2 Processes for responsible use of AI systems; A.9.3 Objectives for responsible use; A.9.4 Intended use of the AI system. Intent: use is governed, bounded to intended use and measured against objectives.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.10 Acceptable use of information and other associated assets; 5.37 Documented operating procedures.
residual_gap: ISO A.9 is the best organisation-level fit for a deployer. Residual: the benchmark is the PROVIDER'S instructions for use (Art. 13) - a certificate does not show you obtained, read and operationalised them.
implementation_note: Keep a per-system register of instructions-for-use versions and the internal procedure each one drives.

obligation_plain_words: Assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training, authority and support.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.3.2 AI roles and responsibilities; A.4.6 Human resources; A.9.2; cl. 7.2 Competence. Intent: named, competent, resourced people.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.2 Information security roles and responsibilities; 6.3 Awareness, education and training.
residual_gap: 'Authority' (the power to override) is the element usually missing in practice and is not a control requirement in either framework. NIST GOVERN 3.2 (differentiating human-AI configuration roles) is the closer outcome.
implementation_note: Document override authority in the role description, not only competence.

obligation_plain_words: To the extent the deployer controls input data, ensure it is relevant and sufficiently representative for the system's intended purpose.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.9.2 Processes for responsible use; A.7.4 Quality of data (development-oriented). Intent: data quality governance.
residual_gap: ISO Annex A data controls (A.7) are written around development data, not live operational inputs. Representativeness for the intended purpose is not tested.
implementation_note: Add input-data checks to the deployer's operating procedure.

obligation_plain_words: Monitor operation on the basis of the instructions for use; where use may present a risk (Art. 79(1)), inform provider/distributor and the market surveillance authority without undue delay and SUSPEND use; for a serious incident, inform first the provider, then importer/distributor and authorities immediately.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.6 Operation and monitoring; A.8.4 Communication of incidents; A.9.2. Intent: watch operation, escalate incidents.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.24-5.27 Incident management; 8.16 Monitoring activities.
residual_gap: The suspend-use duty and the reporting sequence (provider first) are specific legal steps. If the provider cannot be reached, Art. 73 applies mutatis mutandis to the deployer.
implementation_note: Pre-authorise the person who can suspend use; script the notification order.

obligation_plain_words: Before putting into service or using a high-risk system at the workplace, employer-deployers inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to it.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.5 Information for interested parties. Intent: communicate to interested parties.
residual_gap: Collective-information rules sit in national labour law (works councils, consultation). Frameworks do not cover them.
implementation_note: Involve HR and employment counsel per Member State.

obligation_plain_words: Deployers of Annex III systems that make or assist decisions about natural persons must inform those persons that they are subject to the high-risk system.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.5 Information for interested parties; A.8.2 System documentation and information for users. Intent: tell the people affected.
residual_gap: Content, timing and format of the notice are legal choices; ISO intent is generic.
implementation_note: Align with GDPR Art. 13/14/22 notices to avoid inconsistent statements.

obligation_plain_words: Before first use, certain deployers (public-law bodies, private entities providing public services, and deployers of Annex III 5(b) credit-scoring and 5(c) life/health-insurance systems) assess impact on fundamental rights: processes, duration/frequency, affected groups, specific harms, human-oversight implementation, remedies and complaint mechanisms; notify the market surveillance authority with the AI Office template; update when facts change.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Amended: Art. 27(4) deployers may cross-reference existing DPIAs (secondary source; verify OJ text)
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.5.2 AI system impact assessment process; A.5.3 Documentation of impact assessments; A.5.4 Impact on individuals or groups; cl. 6.1.4 / 8.4 AI system impact assessment. Intent: assess and document effects on individuals, groups and society.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.34 Privacy and protection of PII (DPIA interface).
residual_gap: Best conceptual match in the crosswalk (ISO treats impact on individuals as first-class), yet: Art. 27 has a prescribed content list (a)-(f), a scoping rule (who must do it), and a notification-to-authority step with a template. Also: FRIA measures rights, not organisational impact - the register keeps these separate (see /register/).
implementation_note: Use the Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) list as the A.5.3 template; add the authority notification step.

obligation_plain_words: A person affected by a deployer's decision based on output of an Annex III high-risk system (excluding point 2) that has legal or similarly significant adverse effects can obtain clear, meaningful explanations of the AI system's role and the main elements of the decision.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.5 Information for interested parties; A.5.4 Assessing impact on individuals or groups. Intent: communicate with and consider affected people.
residual_gap: An individually enforceable right. Needs a request-handling process and explanation capability; NIST MEASURE 2.9 is about explaining the model for governance, not answering an individual.
implementation_note: Build an explanation-request workflow and measure turnaround.

obligation_plain_words: Before placing a non-EU provider's high-risk system on the market, verify the conformity assessment was done, technical documentation exists, CE marking + EU declaration + instructions for use are present and an authorised representative was appointed; do not place if non-conforming; keep copies 10 years; cooperate with authorities.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.10.3 Suppliers; A.10.2 Allocating responsibilities. Intent: manage what you take in from suppliers.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.19-5.22 Supplier controls.
residual_gap: Importer verification is a legal gate with named documents, not a supplier-assurance process.
implementation_note: Turn Art. 23(1)(a)-(d) into a pre-import checklist.

obligation_plain_words: Before making a high-risk system available, verify CE marking, EU declaration, instructions for use and that provider/importer met their duties; do not supply if non-conforming; take or ensure corrective action; inform authorities where Art. 79(1) risk.
application_date: 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III systems); 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I products). Originally 2 Aug 2026 / 2 Aug 2027.
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.10.2 Allocating responsibilities; A.10.4 Customers. Intent: responsibilities and customer relationships are defined.
residual_gap: As importer: a legal verification gate, not a supplier-management control.
implementation_note: Distributor checklist from Art. 24(1)-(2).

obligation_plain_words: Draw up and keep current technical documentation of the GPAI model (training and testing process, evaluation results; Annex XI items incl. architecture, parameters, data provenance and curation, training compute, energy consumption), to give to the AI Office and national authorities on request. Free and open-source models are exempt unless they carry systemic risk (Art. 53(2)).
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.7 AI system technical documentation; A.6.2.3 Documentation of design and development; A.7.5 Data provenance. Intent: maintain design-level documentation and data lineage.
residual_gap: ISO control is system-oriented; Annex XI is MODEL-oriented (training compute in FLOPs, energy consumption, number of data points). Neither framework asks for energy or compute reporting.
implementation_note: Build the Annex XI sheet as a model card variant and keep it with the model release.

obligation_plain_words: Make information and documentation available to downstream AI-system providers so they understand the model's capabilities and limits and can meet their own obligations (Annex XII: tasks, acceptable-use policy, architecture, modalities, maximum input size, data information, integration means).
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.2 System documentation and information for users; A.8.5 Information for interested parties; A.10.4 Customers. Intent: users and customers get what they need to use the system properly.
residual_gap: Annex XII content list (acceptable use policy, context-window size, integration means) is not in ISO A.8.2. This is the information a downstream provider needs for Art. 25 and Art. 13 - gaps here propagate down the chain.
implementation_note: Publish a downstream pack versioned against model releases.

obligation_plain_words: Put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law, in particular to identify and honour rights reservations expressed under Art. 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790 (including by state-of-the-art technologies).
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.7.3 Acquisition of data; A.7.5 Data provenance. Intent: data is acquired deliberately and traceable. Does not address copyright reservations.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.32 Intellectual property rights.
residual_gap: Honouring machine-readable opt-outs is a specific technical-legal duty. NIST GOVERN 6.1 / MAP 4.1 mention third-party IP infringement risk, which is related but not the Art. 4(3) mechanism.
implementation_note: Document the crawler/opt-out handling and the evidence that it ran.

obligation_plain_words: Draw up and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used to train the model, using the AI Office template.
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.7.5 Data provenance. Intent: internal provenance records - not a public summary.
residual_gap: A PUBLIC disclosure duty. Internal provenance records are an input, not the deliverable. Check the AI Office template version currently in force before publishing.
implementation_note: Generate the public summary from the provenance records and review it with counsel.

obligation_plain_words: Demonstrate compliance through an approved code of practice (until a harmonised standard is published), OR through a harmonised standard (presumption of conformity), OR through alternative adequate means assessed by the Commission.
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model. A voluntary GPAI Code of Practice exists (referenced in secondary sources); verify whether the Commission approved it by implementing act under Art. 56(6).
residual_gap: The GPAI equivalent of the high-risk headline finding: ISO 42001 certification is not one of the three routes the Act names. Without a code or an OJ-cited harmonised standard, the provider carries the burden of showing 'alternative adequate means'.
implementation_note: Decide the compliance route explicitly and record the reasoning.
harmonised_standard_pipeline: No GPAI-specific harmonised standard identified in the JTC 21 tracker used here.

obligation_plain_words: A third-country GPAI provider appoints by written mandate an EU-established authorised representative before placing the model on the Union market (not for open-source models without systemic risk).
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
residual_gap: Statutory appointment; no framework equivalent.
implementation_note: Mandate wording from Art. 54(3)(a)-(d).

obligation_plain_words: For systemic-risk models: perform model evaluation with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including documented adversarial testing to identify and mitigate systemic risks.
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.6.2.4 AI system verification and validation. Intent: validate against requirements - no adversarial/red-team element.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 8.29 Security testing in development and acceptance.
residual_gap: Documented adversarial testing is not an ISO 42001 control. NIST names security/resilience evaluation and independent assessors but not adversarial testing of frontier-scale models as a requirement.
implementation_note: Keep red-team scope, method and results as Annex XI s.2 evidence.

obligation_plain_words: Assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources, arising from development, placing on the market or use of the model.
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: cl. 6.1.2 AI risk assessment; cl. 6.1.4 AI system impact assessment; A.5.5 Assessing societal impacts of AI systems. Intent: assess societal-level impacts.
residual_gap: 'Systemic risk' (Art. 3(65)) is specific to high-impact capabilities with Union-level reach. An organisation-scoped risk assessment will not, by default, be scoped to that.
implementation_note: Add a Union-level systemic-risk register section with named sources.

obligation_plain_words: Track, document and report without undue delay to the AI Office (and, as appropriate, national authorities) serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.8.4 Communication of incidents; A.8.3 External reporting; cl. 10.2. Intent: tell the right parties about incidents.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.24-5.27 Incident management; 5.5 Contact with authorities.
residual_gap: No time limit is given in Art. 55(1)(c) ('without undue delay'), unlike the 15/10/2 day clocks in Art. 73 for high-risk providers. The Act's 'serious incident' definition applies (Art. 3(49)).
implementation_note: Share one incident pipeline across Art. 73 and Art. 55 with the two reporting recipients.

obligation_plain_words: Ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the systemic-risk model and the physical infrastructure of the model.
application_date: Obligations applicable since 2 Aug 2025; Commission fining/enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026; models placed before 2 Aug 2025 must comply by 2 Aug 2027.
omnibus_2026_1744_status: Substantive duties unchanged by Reg. 2026/1744 per secondary sources; AI Office exclusive competence expanded over AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model
iso42001_clause_or_control: A.4.5 System and computing resources. Intent: resourcing - not a security control.
iso27001_2022_supplementary: 5.x Organizational, 7.x Physical and 8.x Technological controls as a set; 8.24 Use of cryptography; 8.3 Information access restriction; 7.1 Physical security perimeters.
residual_gap: The ISMS is the strongest evidence here, but only if its SCOPE statement actually includes model weights, training pipelines and the compute estate - scope is chosen by the organisation and is routinely drawn around corporate IT.
implementation_note: Check the 27001 Statement of Applicability and scope explicitly cover the model assets.
